parole.testo: Borrowed from Greek μαντινάδα (mantináda), from Venetan matinada (“a song of the morning”).

parole.significato: A Greek stew, typically made from rabbit meat, tomatoes, small onions and herbs.
parole.testo: From Greek στιφάδο (stifádo), from Venetan stufado, from Latin extufare, from Ancient Greek τύφος (túphos, “steam”). Compare Italian stufato, French estouffade. Doublet of estouffade.

parole.significato: A Greek dish of tomatoes fried with olive oil, pepper, and beaten eggs.
parole.testo: From Greek στραπατσάδα (strapatsáda), from Venetan strapazzada, from strapazzar (“to treat roughly; to scramble (eggs)”) + -ada (forms verbal nouns). Related to Italian strapazzare.
